subject: MedicaHealth logging: request/response filtering and trace-id handling
messages:
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Olivia Grant <olivia@medicahealth.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 28 Jun 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: MedicaHealth call recap — logging controls and next steps

Hi Olivia — thanks for taking time today. Quick recap from our call and the concrete items we agreed on: 

1) Scope of logs you care about
   - You want request and response bodies for API calls retained for troubleshooting, but any PHI/PII fields scrubbed before long-term storage.
   - Headers: Authorization and cookie headers must be stripped; trace IDs may be considered sensitive if they can link back to internal patient IDs.

2) Residency & retention
   - Preferred residency: US-only (primary region us-east-1).
   - Retention baseline: 30 days for full request/response artifacts, with an option to export/retain aggregated metrics longer.

3) Redaction approach we proposed
   - Ingress-level redaction: strip known sensitive headers and apply regex-based redaction for common PHI fields in bodies.
   - Option to pseudonymize trace IDs by hashing with per-customer salt so they remain linkable for a session but not reversible.

4) Action items
   - Olivia: send a small sample (anonymized or redacted) of typical request/response lines you expect to see (we discussed a 10–20 line sample).
   - Olga/Redwood: provide a 1-page summary of proposed filtering (ingress rules, retention defaults, pseudonymization option) and SOC2 evidence we can share.
   - Redwood eng/security: confirm feasibility and timeline for a gated POC showing hashed trace ids + ingress header drop.

Attachments: I attached a short example snippet format (medica_sample_reqres_snippet.json) to show the shape we had in mind. Also attaching a draft one-pager I will circulate to the team (redaction-proposal-v1.pdf).

Proposed next step: 30-minute technical demo/POC on Wednesday 7/7 or Thursday 7/8 — does either work for you?

Thanks again — I’ll follow up internally to pull engineering and security into the loop.

Best,
Olga
Director, Solutions Engineering
Redwood Inference

Hi Olivia, Olga, and Neha — thanks for the clear notes. Quick engineering/security confirmation for the POC/demo on Thu 7/8: 

1) Hashing/pseudonymization
   - We can implement deterministic hashing using a per-customer HMAC-SHA256 with a KMS-managed key (salt). This yields non-reversible identifiers for our service and still allows session correlation. We will document the threat model: hashes are not reversible without the KMS key; key access is audited and restricted.

2) Ingress redaction & header filtering
   - Edge filter can drop Authorization/Cookie/Set-Cookie headers and apply a small configurable rule-set for body redaction (regex + field allowlist). Latency impact: expected median <5ms; 95th percentile in our lab ~15–22ms depending on payload size (we’ll measure against Medica sample).

3) Residency & retention
   - We can route filtered artifacts to a US-only storage partition and enforce a 30-day TTL. Longer aggregate metrics can be exported to a separate reporting store on request.

4) Artifacts for procurement
   - Attaching a short SOC2 controls summary (soc2-summary.pdf) and the one-page redaction proposal. We can also provide a short network diagram for how logs flow through the edge -> filter -> US storage; I will include that in the demo slides.

POC runbook (high level):
   a) Ingest sample (you provide) into our staging ingestion pipeline with the ingress filter turned on.
   b) Verify hashed trace ids and header drops via a QA job (we’ll produce a masked sample).
   c) Review retention behavior and export path.

We’re good to demo Thu 7/8 at 10:00am PT. I’ll send a calendar invite with dial-in + a short agenda and a link to a shared drive where we’ll drop artifacts.

Best,
Sean Gallagher
Security & Trust
Redwood Inference
